Latin America & Caribbean Subset

The analysis below restricts the dataset to Latin American and Caribbean countries only. This is the region where dengue is endemic and where the comparison is epidemiologically meaningful. Non-endemic countries (France, Spain, UK, USA, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Thailand) are excluded because their reported cases are dominated by travel-associated infections, not local transmission.

Interpretation

  • Spearman’s Rho (\(\rho\)): A value close to 1 indicates a strong positive relationship, -1 indicates a strong negative relationship, and 0 indicates no relationship.
  • P-value: If the p-value is less than 0.05, the correlation is statistically significant. Given the sparse nature of this mixed dataset, a high p-value suggests we cannot rule out that any apparent pattern is due to random chance.

Notes

  • The x-axis and y-axis are both on log scales.

Blind

1. Summary

Last week I ran the OBAMA (Optimization-Based Analysis of Multiple Arrays) tool on the duck microbiome dataset provided by Dr. Lourdes Peña Castillo. Instead of using the original disease.state grouping (control vs. disease), I regrouped the samples using the rfi_group column from the metadata file, which classifies birds by Residual Feed Intake (RFI) — A_high (less feed-efficient) vs. B_low (more feed-efficient). This produces a biologically meaningful comparison for a feed-efficiency study rather than a disease-status one.

2. Files Received

Three files were provided for this analysis:

File Contents
duck_otu_relative_abundance_20.tsv Relative abundance table of bacterial genera per sample. Columns: geo_accession, disease.state, and ~300 g__* taxa columns.
duck_otu_presence_absence_20.tsv Binary (0/1) presence–absence matrix for the same taxa across the same samples.
duck_metadata_20.tsv Sample metadata. Columns: run_accession, sample_alias, duck_id, segment, rfi_group.

3. Metadata Grouping

The metadata file contains a rfi_group column with two levels:

  • A_high — high RFI (less feed-efficient birds)
  • B_low — low RFI (more feed-efficient birds)

All 20 samples are jejunum segment samples. This grouping was used in place of disease.state for the OBAMA run.

4. OBAMA MCO Results

The Multi-Criteria Optimization (MCO) module returned 44 taxa distributed across 10 Pareto frontiers, where frontier 1 represents the most optimal trade-off between the two performance metrics (Median and Mean relative abundance).

4.1 Frontier 1 Taxa

The six taxa on the most optimal frontier are:

  • g__Acinetobacter
  • g__Bradyrhizobium_503403
  • g__Helicobacter_G
  • g__Romboutsia_B
  • g__Rothia
  • g__Staphylococcus

5. Biological Interpretation

  • Butyrate producers — Blautia_A_141781 (frontier 5), Mediterraneibacter_A_155507 (frontier 7), Faecalibacillus (frontier 8). These Firmicutes are consistently enriched in low-RFI (efficient) birds in the literature.
  • Romboutsia is a known RFI-associated genus. A 2024 study on ducks during high production period found that RFI “particularly affecting metabolism and disease-related microorganisms such as Romboutsia, Enterococcus, and Megamonas funiformis” . The fact that Romboutsia_B appears on Frontier 1 is a strong validation signal.
  • Lactic acid bacteria — Ligilactobacillus (frontier 4), Bifidobacterium_388775 (frontier 8). Associated with gut health and improved energy harvest.
  • Environmental / noise taxa — Bradyrhizobium_503403, Pelomonas, Brevundimonas, Acinetobacter. These appear on the frontier but are probably transient gut passengers rather than true residents; their appearance is strange and warrants investigation.

The presence of butyrate producers on lower frontiers is the strongest signal supporting a real feed-efficiency effect in the microbiome.

Limitation: Missing Sex Data
